title: 20(R)-Rg3 derived from ginseng fibrous roots ameliorates DSS-induced colitis via selective modulation of glucocorticoid receptor signaling.
authors: Kong, Xinyu; Wang, Pei; Zhang, Shumin; Kou, Lijuan; Tan, Mengxia; Xie, Zeping; Guo, Wei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究人参皂苷20(R)-Rg3通过糖皮质激素受体信号缓解结肠炎，核心是蛋白-小分子互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法用于TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Naturally derived selective glucocorticoid receptor (GR) modulators dissociate anti-inflammatory efficacy from adverse effects. Rare ginsenosides have emerged as promising candidates for this selective modulation. This study explored rare ginsenosides derived from ginseng fibrous roots to evaluate their ability to selectively influence GR signaling. Rare ginsenosides were prepared from ginseng fibrous roots via alcoholic extraction, followed by targeted acid hydrolysis. Selective GR modulators were screened using a combination of molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and cellular assays. The selective regulation of GR signaling was further validated in a DSS-induced murine colitis model using dexamethasone (DEX) as a positive control. Four rare ginsenosides, 20(R)-Rg3, 20(S)-Rg3, Rk1, and Rg5, were obtained. Computational analyses revealed that 20(R)-Rg3 bound strongly and stably to GR. In cellular models, 20(R)-Rg3 promoted GR nuclear translocation and suppressed inflammatory responses by reducing NO, IL-6 and TNF-alpha production. Notably, 20(R)-Rg3 selectively induced GR-mediated transrepression by inhibiting NF-kappaBRE-dependent transcription without activating GRE-driven transactivation, identifying it as a functionally selective GR modulator. In vivo oral administration of 20(R)-Rg3 significantly alleviated colonic inflammation, as evidenced by clinical signs, colon histopathology, serum TNF-alpha and IL-6 levels, together with colonic MPO activity and phosphorylated levels of NF-kappaB p65 and IkappaBalpha. High-dose 20(R)-Rg3 exhibited efficacy comparable to that of dexamethasone while preserving thymus and spleen integrity and avoiding the induction of GR transactivation-associated metabolic genes (TAT and PEPCK). These results demonstrate that 20(R)-Rg3, derived from ginseng fibrous roots, functions as a natural selective GR modulator with anti-inflammatory activity. Its ability to dissociate therapeutic efficacy from systemic side effects highlights its potential as a safer alternative to conventional corticosteroids in management of inflammatory diseases.
abstract_zh: 天然来源的选择性糖皮质激素受体（GR）调节剂可将抗炎疗效与不良反应分离。稀有人参皂苷已成为此类选择性调节的有前景候选物。本研究探讨了源自人参须根的稀有人参皂苷，以评估其选择性影响GR信号传导的能力。通过醇提法从人参须根中制备稀有人参皂苷，随后进行靶向酸水解。利用分子对接、分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟和细胞实验的组合筛选选择性GR调节剂。在DSS诱导的小鼠结肠炎模型中，以地塞米松（DEX）作为阳性对照，进一步验证了GR信号的选择性调节。获得了四种稀有人参皂苷：20(R)-Rg3、20(S)-Rg3、Rk1和Rg5。计算分析显示，20(R)-Rg3与GR结合强烈且稳定。在细胞模型中，20(R)-Rg3促进GR核转位，并通过减少NO、IL-6和TNF-α的产生抑制炎症反应。值得注意的是，20(R)-Rg3通过抑制NF-κB依赖性转录选择性诱导GR介导的转抑制，而不激活GRE驱动的转激活，从而将其鉴定为功能性选择性GR调节剂。体内口服20(R)-Rg3显著缓解结肠炎症，这通过临床体征、结肠组织病理学、血清TNF-α和IL-6水平，以及结肠MPO活性和NF-κB p65与IκBα的磷酸化水平得以证实。高剂量20(R)-Rg3表现出与地塞米松相当的疗效，同时保持胸腺和脾脏完整性，并避免诱导GR转激活相关的代谢基因（TAT和PEPCK）。这些结果表明，源自人参须根的20(R)-Rg3作为一种具有抗炎活性的天然选择性GR调节剂。其将治疗效果与全身副作用分离的能力，凸显了其作为传统皮质类固醇在炎症性疾病管理中更安全替代品的潜力。
